summary.oneLiner: PPAP Automotive marked a strategic inflection point in Q4FY26 via a INR100cr JV divestment and rebranding to 'Ajay Group', driving a 25.7% QoQ revenue recovery to INR174.6cr despite one-off labor code costs. The narrative shifts from pure auto-cyclicality to diversified growth led by a 36% aftermarket surge, imminent battery breakeven, and sharper focus through vertical hiving/mergers.

one-line thesis: PPAP Automotive marked a strategic inflection point in Q4FY26 via a INR100cr JV divestment and rebranding to 'Ajay Group', driving a 25.7% QoQ revenue recovery to INR174.6cr despite one-off labor code costs. The narrative shifts from pure auto-cyclicality to diversified growth led by a 36% aftermarket surge, imminent battery breakeven, and sharper focus through vertical hiving/mergers.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR174.6cr (Q4, +18.6% YoY, +25.7% QoQ); FY26 Rev: INR567cr. EBITDA: INR16.9cr (+12.9% YoY); Margin ~9.7% (impacted by one-offs). PAT: Impacted by INR3.6cr one-time employee benefit obligation (Labor Code) and mark-to-market investment losses; normalized margins improved to ~13% ex-one-offs. Order Book: INR840cr new business secured in FY26; execution over 3-5 years. Net Debt: Reduced to INR103cr post-divestment proceeds (Gross Debt INR195cr).
guidance: FY27 guidance deferred to Q1FY27 results due to geopolitical/raw material volatility. Implicit targets: Capacity utilization >80-82%; Battery segment PBT profitable; Tooling capacity doubling to ~300 molds/year over 3 years.
order book & pipeline: INR840cr new orders secured in FY26 across EV/ICE; diversified across Maruti, Tata, Mahindra, Honda, Kia, VinFast, Euler Motors; lifetime execution window 3-5 years.
segment / subsidiary detail: Auto Parts: Core revenue driver; new SOPs for SUVs/EVs ramping. Aftermarket: +36% YoY growth; 147 distributors, 1,264 SKUs. Tooling: +12.1% growth; 148 molds developed; >90% utilization. Industrial Products: +38% growth via exports/non-auto. Batteries: Revenue up 1.28x YoY; Q4 loss narrowed to INR40L (vs INR1.2cr prior year); targeting 100% utilization in FY27.
growth verticals / optionality: Aftermarket expansion (25%+ CAGR target); Battery segment turnaround (profitable PBT expected FY27); Tooling scale-up (double capacity); New OEM wins (VinFast, Euler, Kia, Mahindra) shifting portfolio to 90% SUVs.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 EBITDA margin ~9.7% suppressed by INR3.6cr labor code one-off; underlying operational margin ~13%. Raw material inflation ongoing; 50% pass-through achieved, balance under negotiation. Cost mitigation via solar energy adoption and employee reforms planned.
capex / expansion: Future capex to be funded via internal accruals; no immediate debt increase planned. Strategic funds from JV divestment (INR100cr) reserved for M&A or strategic investments, not routine capex.
capital allocation: Divestment proceeds (INR100cr) allocated to strengthen reserves, reduce net debt (to INR103cr), and fund future strategic opportunities. Final dividend INR1.5/share (Total FY26: INR2.5/share).
risks & watch-items: West Asia conflict disrupting logistics and elevating raw material costs. Delayed SOPs from specific OEM models (now resolving). Regulatory delays in subsidiary merger/hive-off approvals. Entry-level sedan demand weakness (mitigated by SUV shift).
management quality / tone: Cautiously Optimistic; Transparent on one-offs; Strategic/Restructuring-focused; Emphasizing operational efficiency and portfolio rebalancing towards high-growth verticals.
non-obvious takeaways: Rebranding to 'Ajay Group' signals a holistic conglomerate strategy beyond just 'PPAP'. The battery unit's rapid loss reduction (INR1.2cr to INR40L in one year) suggests a faster-than-expected turnaround trajectory. 78% of revenue now comes from vehicles <5 years old, reducing obsolescence risk.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
